candidate_relations.reason: The IHC profile (ER−, PR−, HER2−) is consistent with triple-negative status, and lymphoepithelioma-like carcinoma of the breast is indeed triple-negative, but 'triple-negative breast cancer' is a parent/molecular category that lacks the defining histological specificity (cohesive nests within dense lymphoid infiltrate) required by the reference diagnosis
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Triple-negative breast cancer is a broad molecular subtype; lymphoepithelioma-like carcinoma of the breast is a rare specific histological subtype that happens to be triple-negative, but the reference requires the specific histological designation

candidate_relations.label: Medullary breast cancer, left breast
candidate_relations.reason: While medullary carcinoma is a reasonable differential given the lymphoid infiltrate and triple-negative status, it is a separate and incompatible histological subtype from lymphoepithelioma-like carcinoma; asserting medullary carcinoma conflicts with the specific reference diagnosis
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Medullary carcinoma shares some overlapping features (lymphoid infiltrate, triple-negative profile) but is a distinct histological entity with different architectural criteria (syncytial growth, pushing borders, moderate-to-marked lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate) compared to lymphoepithelioma-like carcinoma which shows cohesive nests within a dense lymphoid stroma resembling nasopharyngeal lymphoepithelioma

case_quality_flags: Lymphoepithelioma-like carcinoma of the breast is a very rare entity; the histological description (cohesive nests of neoplastic epithelial cells within dense lymphoid infiltrate with CD3/CD20-positive background lymphocytes and cytokeratin-positive epithelial cells) is classic and distinguishes it from medullary carcinoma
